d.d: Any animal belonging to the Suidae family of mammals, especially the pig, the warthog, and the boar.
An adult swine, at or above a certain body weight.
A greedy person or thing; one who refuses to share; a gluttonous one.
To greedily take more than one's share, to take precedence at the expense of another or others.
d.x: Hey! Quit hogging all the blankets.

d.d: To clip the mane of a horse, making it short and bristly.
(of a hedge) to trim up closely
A one-room Native American (especially Navajo) dwelling or lodge, constructed of wood and earth and covered with mud.
A young sheep of either sex, until it cuts its first two teeth.
d.x: They sent a lorryload of hoggs to the auction mart, and they will keep the rest for their own flock.

d.d: present participle and gerund of hog
Taking up too much of something so others cannot use it.
d.x: The child was hogging the arcade game.

d.d: Making a rough cut to quickly remove material
Drooping at the ends; arching; in distinction from sagging.
d.x: For a cantilevered beam, the steel reinforcement should be placed at the top to carry the hogging moment along the upper face.

d.d: third-person singular simple present indicative of hog
A mixture of solid and liquid food scraps fed to pigs; swill.
